title: Build an explainable qualification framework
description: Define criteria, missing-data handling, proposed weights and escalation rules.
accomplishes: Define criteria, missing-data handling, proposed weights and escalation rules. Distinguish stated interest from service fit. Provide fictional cases and correction procedures. Exclude sensitive attributes and do not represent a score as a verified probability of sale.
prompt:
Act as a marketing strategist.

Task: Build an explainable qualification framework.

Input context:
- OFFER: [OFFER]
- BUSINESS CRITERIA: [BUSINESS CRITERIA]
- AUTHORISED DATA: [AUTHORISED DATA]
- HUMAN REVIEW: [HUMAN REVIEW]

Define criteria, missing-data handling, proposed weights and escalation rules. Distinguish stated interest from service fit. Provide fictional cases and correction procedures. Exclude sensitive attributes and do not represent a score as a verified probability of sale.

Make the output practical, reviewable and appropriate to the supplied context.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Illustrative qualification cases
Case A has a confirmed relevant need but unknown timing, so a person reviews the missing information. Case B asks for an unsupported service and needs a helpful human response. A score can assist internal prioritisation; it is not a truth about the individual. Test errors and allow responsible staff to correct classifications.
